Question Choices: What is the least common denominator of 1/(x - 3) and 1/(x + 3)?
Hints: The factors are distinct.;Multiply them together.
Solution: Factor the polynomials: x - 3 and x + 3. Take every distinct factor at its greatest exponent to obtain (x - 3)*(x + 3). It is divisible by each original polynomial with no unnecessary factors. When used as a common denominator, exclude all zeros of either original denominator.
